previous_talk.title: How to run 100 agents in parallel and keep your sanity
previous_talk.summary: The talk applies manufacturing constraints to agent workflows: trigger, plan, code, review, merge. It treats merged PRs as a delivery proxy, identifies review as a bottleneck in the example, and argues for increasing capacity across the whole line. It discusses event triggers, planning context, parallel environments, tests, agent review and visual validation. The Q&A retains human intent and architectural judgment as review boundaries.

sources.text:
Here is the result of "fetch" for the Page with URL https://app.notion.com/p/f42b9d5bf61682a0ab6c813e7d7fbcce as of 2026-07-15T16:34:11.906Z: {"title":"Kiet’s Q3 Product Roadmap"} null # Vision Agents are now there, the bottle neck for a 10-person \$1B company is no longer intelligence, its collecting the techniques and infrastructure required to run a large org with less engineers. We should not build a software factory initially. Instead, we build the building blocks for our users to build the factory. Our first users has always been ourselves and the parts of the product that flop are things we don’t use ourselves: - Linear - Chat GUI - Remote workspaces - CLI (initially)

The question becomes:

What are the building blocks we should create for the factory? ### Building blocks #### 1. Triggers

Trigger is the starting point of the whole process, this can be a schedule, a manual

Example: - Automation - Webhook/trigger - Manual trigger

It should also allow for moving from 1 stage of the factory into the next.

#### 2. Workspace The environment in which the agent + human can do the work, inspection of the work, etc. It could also be used to do verification, review, etc. Example: - Local worktree - Cloud sandbox #### 3. Memory A way to glue the stages and pieces of the factory together and to continuously improve the factory. It can be as simple as docs that the agents at each step can refer to or fancy skills and MCPs #### 4. Visibility No factories can be viable without very good metrics and data to which the factory can be tuned and improved. This can include dashboards, review, tuning

## What’s the end state?

In 12 months, an engineer using Superset uses it like so:

They find out about Superset through people talking about how it 10x their development flow

They onboard to the product and is immediately productive.

It takes an intent they have: “Given my project, I want to ship feature A”.

It allows them to use the best state of the art model for everything.

While it’s shipping, they are prompted once again: “what do you want to do next?” “Given my project, I want to ship feature B”. It goes and does it, prompting them again.

They are able to see both features and their current state, it prompts them when they need to add input, saves or offers to save learnings as it goes. Helping them all the way until the feature is merged.

Once they’re comfortable and have time again, it prompts them to continue doing, or hook up automations like triggers, etc. It then ingests their tasks, give some candidates to scale up.

If they scale too fast it warns them about throughput. They scale up slowly while keeping quality high. They 10x their development. They bring it into their org, each member adds more throughput but still own their own flow. The whole factory gets better over time. Within a few weeks the whole org is shipping 10x more.

What do we ship now?

Working backwards from the vision, we want to get to the final state:
  • Fully functional factory
    • Trigger goes all the way to PR
    • Minimal human interaction, only at important points
    • Good review and inspection
    • Good metrics on the factory and throughput
    • Self-improving given metrics
  • Current state - Manual trigger - Heavy human interaction - No visibility in defect and throughput - No self-improvement - Manual review and inspection
### Goes into buckets: - Trigger - Integrations - Linear + other ticketing - First class Slack + Discord bot support - Automations
  • Needs a lot more work and needs to be a bigger part of the experience
- Review - Agent-driven review - Artifacts and better UI - Visibility - Merge rate - Cost - Dwell time - Policies on how long something dwells - Defect rate - Etc. - Self-improving - Knowledge is stored and iterated on - Can just be markdown files or docs - Workspace - Cloud sandboxes #### How to spend the next 3 months? - Build the primitives - Improve the core part of the business - Cut un-needed parts

sources.text:
Here is the result of "fetch" for the Page with URL https://app.notion.com/p/3a4b9d5bf61680728eb5fe57fc3cd872 as of 2026-10-06T21:38:27.056Z: {"title":"Homework (Kiet) 1"} {"type":"emoji","emoji":"📔"} # Purpose The purpose of this exercise is to maximize the quality of our planning discussion. We can document independently before reading anyone else’s responses. We’re not necessarily trying to build a consensus we’re trying to surface the strongest ideas, disagreements, assumptions, opportunities estimated time: 2-3hrs. ---
  • Duplicate this page and add it to the Planning Exercise document
  • Be specific and opinionated
  • Complete independently
  • Try best to separate evidence from assumptions and focus on the ideas you think matter most
--- 1\. Twelve-Month Success

What are the three most important outcomes Superset should achieve over the next 12 months?

Example: Engineering teams move materially faster when using Superset. ### Outcome 1 - Self improving software factory Outcome: Engineering teams can run self-improving software factory with superset Why it matters:

Self-improving because it’s a runaway advantage. Makes it hard to switch from and once you’re in superset your experience keeps getting better.

How we would know it happened: Teams continuously increase PR merge rate while engineers spend constant or less time/interaction per PR --- ### Outcome 2 - The single workspace Outcome: Superset can be used to drive all of an engineer’s work. Including browser and computer use to get anything they need. Why it matters: We don’t want any reason for users to leave the app at all. There’s no structural reason we couldn’t do this either. How we would know it happened:

Users spend more and more of their time in the app and the diversity of work they do in superset changes to include most of their other work. Like triaging, reviewing, CI, etc.

--- ### Outcome 3 - Teams Outcome: Superset becomes the way that teams manage their engineering. Why it matters:

Most serious engineering is done within teams, right now the ecosystem is very fragmented. Teams all need this.

How we would know it happened: We have high saturation within teams and they all use superset as their main driver.

--- 2\. Biggest Opportunities List your 5 highest-leverage ideas. For each opportunity, include: - Description: What would we build or change? - Problem: What problem does it solve? - Customer value: How would it improve the customer’s experience or results? - Company value: How could it improve adoption, retention, revenue, differentiation, or learning? - Outcome supported: Which 12-month outcome does it advance? - Strategic importance: Why is this important to Superset specifically? - Confidence: this will deliver value described: Low, medium, or high - Estimated effort: Small, medium, or large - Risks: What could make this fail or become more expensive than expected?
Opportunity 1 - Software factory Description: Software factory Problem: Writing software is still very manual right now. But not in the right way. Users are typing the same prompt and clicking the same buttons and wasting a lot of time. Customer value: Users save time and become 10x more productive, spending their time where it matters. Company value: Increase adoption Outcome supported: #1, Self improving software factory Strategic importance: It’s the future and mission of the company Confidence: High Estimated effort: Large Risks:

Someone gets there first. Or we’re first but people catch up.

There’s a chance it’s not possible or useful. Users don’t want it. Opportunity 2 - Self improving Description: Self improving loops Problem:

Users learnings aren’t being saved and introspected on, especially across agents. I still manually or tell the agents so save learnings when they should not need me to.

Customer value: Users save time and get better results over time Company value: More adoption Outcome supported: #1, Self improving software factory Strategic importance: Learnings for users can be shared across everyone, creating massive moat Differentiation as no one is doing this Confidence: High Estimated effort: High Risks:

Not being able to do it well. Spend a lot of effort on it just for model labs to do it better.

Opportunity 3 - Single workspace Description: Be the single point of entry for any engineering work Problem: Users still have to leave the platform to review code, check CI, use the browser, etc. Customer value: Users don’t need to context switch for anything Company value: More usage, more engagement Outcome supported: #2 Single workspace you need Strategic importance: Users are more engaged Confidence: Medium Estimated effort: Medium Risks: Scope expansion and lack of ability to achieve it Opportunity 4 - Teams Description: Superset for teams Problem: Engineering with AI between team members is still unsolved and annoying learnings aren’t easily shared between team members Customer value: Teams can all get better together and work better + faster Company value: Huge advantage for teams, easier buy Outcome supported: #3 Teams Strategic importance: It’s harder for a full team to churn, especially when they invest their workflows and processes into superset Confidence: High Estimated effort: High Risks: Diluting the individual users’ performance. Not achieving enough buy-in per team to get value Opportunity 5 - Open orchestrator Description: The truly open orchestrator between agents Problem: Using the app is still manual, users still interact directly with agents. Platform risks for users to use a single provider / agent Customer value:

Customers aren’t locked into 1 solution, less risk. They’re also able to use open models, etc.

Company value: Cost savings, better performance and access to latest and greatest Outcome supported: #2 Single workspace Strategic importance:

It’s how we wouldn’t get squished by the model labs

Confidence: Low Estimated effort: Medium Risks: Still very competitive, there are many small players. Single lab can still dominate and we’d lose because there’s no competition 3\. Rank your proposed opportunities from highest priority to lowest:
1. Software factory
2. Self improving
3. Single workspace
4. Teams
5. Open orchestrator 4\. What we should NOT build now List five ideas that should not be prioritized during the next 12 months. This could include Features, customer segments, integrations 1. All of the integrations 1. Why not now - We should do a small list of most important but it’s not feasible to maintain without large team 2. What could cause us to reconsider - Once we have more engineering efforts or some high value integrations might be worth it 2. Remote workspace 1. Why not now - Not useful enough to enough users, highly complex 2. What could cause us to reconsider - If there’s real large customer demands for self-hosting remote workspaces 3. Real-time 1. Why not now - Not useful enough to enough users, highly complex 2. What could cause us to reconsider - Once real big teams are asking for it For each: - Idea - Why not now - What could cause us to reconsider 5\. Strategic Advantages

List everything you think our durable advantages:

1. Optimized and polished product 2. Lots of money while being very small 3. Got 2 enterprise contracts 4. Well known product in the niche 5. Open source 6. No data yet but we could 7. Speed 6\. Success Metrics List what you think our top 3 success metrics you think we should care about: 1. Revenue 2. DAU 3. Enterprise contracts signed 7\. Reflection Finish these sentences:
  1. The most important strategic bet 1. Self-improving software factory
  2. The top quarterly priority 1. Get there while bringing our users along
  3. I think the team underestimates 1. How quickly we can get there
  4. I think the team overestimates 1. How much work getting a factory locally is
---

[ ] Orchestration Chat - [x] Managed Cloud Experience - [x] Mobile - [x] Usage based Pricing/Token Tracking ## Exit criteria (draft — ratify in planning) - Cloud workspace ready ≤10s from click; sandbox-backed workspaces GA'd - Linear ticket → workspace → PR-with-proof loop live - Full workspace/agent lifecycle drivable via CLI + SDK; an agent can spawn a reviewer subagent - Usage tier live with metering; first usage MRR ## In this cycle - Sandboxes — isolated, machine-unbound environments; replaces the hosts architecture - Shared cloud environments — cloud workspaces as shared team environments - Superset SDK / API — the public integration surface, mirroring the CLI 1:1 - Full headless support through CLI — scripted control; agents spawn agents - Native Tasks System — assign agent work through Linear, report results back - Sandbox permissions — see open decisions - Superset Mobile — see open decisions - Usage-based billing — metering + invoicing; prereq for router take-rate - Cloud backed chat → Stored in cloud - SOP/Artifact/MD files/Processes & Systems → Build in opinions about introspection and self improving → introspect to figure out what processes should be codified → Figure out how to make a recursive loop ## Open decisions - This is two cycles in one. Eight projects (five M/L) spanning cloud infra + mobile + monetization won't fit 4 weeks. Proposal: keep the substrate (Sandboxes, SDK/API, Headless CLI, Native Tasks) and split Monetization (usage billing → token tracking) and Mobile into their own later cycles. - "Orchestration Chat" is in scope here but its project row lives in First Production Line — reconcile. - Sandbox permissions was explicitly "wait for enterprise to ask" — in or out?

# Questions:

  • Figure out what the use case is for web

sources.text:
Here is the result of "fetch" for the Page with URL https://app.notion.com/p/3b4b9d5bf61680b9aaf8cbc08745b905 as of 2026-10-05T05:11:33.831Z: {"title":"Video notes"} null # CLI Video Series — 2 videos Video 1 = you drive the CLI (\~3 min). Video 2 = your agent drives it (\~3 min). Demo project: demo-app at ~/workplace/demo-app — planted bug: login redirects to /dashbord (typo) → 404. Live IDs: - Project: e1a9e739-01ec-4068-8dd0-b3fb96b89854 - Workspace fix-login-bug: 9c2fa0b2-e746-479f-8e0d-52c57e046fe8 - Claude session: c9c6b51e-5749-4072-83ec-d6ac3a4ac40c - Automation: 66598ed3-aae1-48ca-9476-e43c3c9173ea (paused — resume before filming) --- ## Video 1 — The Superset CLI ### 1. Cold open Usually you can use the superset app from the app UI. But you can drive it all from the terminal using our CLI. Here’s a single command to create a new workspace, and spin up claude code to fix a bug

Then: "One command. Isolated workspace, agent already working on the bug." ```bash superset workspaces create \ --project e1a9e739-01ec-4068-8dd0-b3fb96b89854 \ --name "fix-login-bug" \ --branch fix/login-bug \ --local \ --agent claude \ --prompt "Signing in lands on a 404. Fix the login redirect bug and add a regression test." ``` Show: the bug first — npm start, Sign in, 404. Then run it. Hard cut. ### 2. Setup — once, 30 seconds Say: "Install, sign in, done." ```bash brew install superset-sh/tap/superset superset auth login ``` ### 3. Point it at your repo Say: "Use the checkout you already have." ```bash superset projects create --name "demo-app" --local --import ~/workplace/demo-app ``` ### 4. The one command, explained Say: "Own branch, own worktree — your checkout is untouched. And it's all in the app." ```bash superset workspaces open 9c2fa0b2-e746-479f-8e0d-52c57e046fe8 ``` Show: desktop app opens on the workspace, Claude working in the pane. ### 5. Steer from any terminal Say: "Glance at it. Redirect it. Never interrupt it." ```bash superset terminals read \ --workspace 9c2fa0b2-e746-479f-8e0d-52c57e046fe8 \ --terminal c9c6b51e-5749-4072-83ec-d6ac3a4ac40c --max-lines 100 ``` ```bash superset terminals send \ --workspace 9c2fa0b2-e746-479f-8e0d-52c57e046fe8 \ --terminal c9c6b51e-5749-4072-83ec-d6ac3a4ac40c \ --text "Also update the README known-issues section once it's fixed" ``` ### 6. Finale Say: "Review it like any teammate's branch. Next video: the agent runs these commands instead of you." Show: restart app → Sign in → dashboard. --- ## Video 2 — Your agent drives Superset ### 1. Give your agent the skills Say (over the first frame): "Last video you drove the Superset CLI. This time, your agent drives it." Then: "Skills teach your agent the CLI. Desktop users already have them." ```bash npx skills add superset-sh/skills ``` ### 2. Ask for parallel work — the centerpiece Say: "Plain English. It spins up a workspace per worker, launches agents, collects results — everything from Video 1, run by your agent." Type in Claude Code: > Use the superset:orchestrate skill. Split this work into 3 independent slices, run a worker on each in its own workspace, and report back when all workers are done or blocked. Show: workspaces popping into the sidebar, workers running in parallel. ### 3. Put it on a schedule Say: "A nightly agent in one command." ```bash superset automations create --name "Nightly audit" \ --project e1a9e739-01ec-4068-8dd0-b3fb96b89854 \ --rrule "FREQ=DAILY;BYHOUR=2;BYMINUTE=0" \ --prompt "Audit yesterday's merged PRs for missing tests and file tasks" superset automations run 66598ed3-aae1-48ca-9476-e43c3c9173ea ``` ### 4. Outro Say: "Beta, moving fast. [docs.superset.sh/cli](http://docs.superset.sh/cli)." --- ## Gotchas (off-camera) - Resume the automation before filming: superset automations resume 66598ed3-aae1-48ca-9476-e43c3c9173ea - automations create has no --local flag — host defaults to this machine. - Beats 1/3 create things that already exist — delete first for a clean take; fresh runs print new IDs. - Bug lives on main; the fix lands on fix/login-bug — the 404 demo stays reproducible. --- ## Feats of strength (b-roll / power shots) ### 1. Race three agents on the same bug ```bash for agent in claude codex opencode; do superset workspaces create \ --project e1a9e739-01ec-4068-8dd0-b3fb96b89854 \ --name "race-$agent" --branch "race/$agent" --local \ --agent "$agent" \ --prompt "Signing in lands on a 404. Fix the login redirect bug and add a regression test." done ``` ### 2. Fan out five identical workers ```bash for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do superset workspaces create \ --project e1a9e739-01ec-4068-8dd0-b3fb96b89854 \ --name "worker-$i" --branch "worker/$i" --local \ --agent claude \ --prompt "Signing in lands on a 404. Fix the login redirect bug and add a regression test." done ``` ### 3. Read the entire fleet at once (tested, works) ```bash superset workspaces list --project demo-app --quiet | while read ws; do superset terminals list --workspace "$ws" --json 2>/dev/null \ | jq -r '.sessions[].terminalId' | while read t; do echo "=== $ws / $t ===" superset terminals read --workspace "$ws" --terminal "$t" --max-lines 5 --json | jq -r '.text' done done ``` ### 4. Broadcast an order to every running agent ```bash superset workspaces list --project demo-app --quiet | while read ws; do superset terminals list --workspace "$ws" --json 2>/dev/null \ | jq -r '.sessions[].terminalId' | while read t; do superset terminals send --workspace "$ws" --terminal "$t" \ --text "Status check: summarize what you have done and what remains in 2 sentences." done done ``` ### 5. Create an automation and fire it immediately, one pipe ```bash superset automations create --name "Hourly health check" \ --project e1a9e739-01ec-4068-8dd0-b3fb96b89854 \ --rrule "FREQ=HOURLY" \ --prompt "Run the test suite; if anything fails, file a task with the failure output." \ --json | jq -r '.id' | xargs -I{} superset automations run {} ``` Camera notes: - #2 launches 5 real Claude sessions — sidebar filling up is the money shot. Cleanup after: superset workspaces list --project demo-app --quiet | xargs -L1 superset workspaces delete (spares main). - #4 sends to every terminal including plain shells — looks best when the fleet is all agents. - #5 leaves an hourly automation running — pause or delete it after the take.
